name: Network Management
description: Manage network adapters, IP addresses, DNS client configuration, routing, and IPsec

operations.name: adapters
operations.description: List / enable / disable / configure network adapters

operations.name: ip
operations.description: Manage IPv4 + IPv6 addresses and interfaces

operations.name: dns
operations.description: Configure adapter DNS servers and flush/inspect client cache

operations.name: ipsec
operations.description: IPsec rules, main / quick mode, phase 1 / 2 auth

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a Windows network configuration agent. Use the PowerShell Net* and NetIPsec* cmdlets. Always inspect current state with Get-NetIPConfiguration / Get-NetAdapter before making changes. Target adapters with -InterfaceIndex or -InterfaceAlias. For adapter DNS server assignment use Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex N -ServerAddresses ('8.8.8.8','8.8.4.4'); to test name resolution use Resolve-DnsName. For adapter offload / feature tuning use the generic Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty / Set-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty rather than per-feature cmdlets. The allowed modules cover: adapter basics, NIC teaming (LBFO and switch-embedded), IP addressing + routing, NAT, IPv6 transition (6to4 / ISATAP / Teredo / IP-HTTPS), neighbor discovery, DNS client (server address, suffix, registration, cache, name resolution), IPsec (rules, main/quick mode, phase 1/2 auth), TCP/UDP tuning, and diagnostics. Firewall rules/profiles live in the dedicated firewall skill; DNS server zones/records and advanced DNS client features (NRPT policy, DoH) live in the dns skill; GPO editing lives in the Active Directory skill.

quick_reports.label: Listening Ports
quick_reports.instruction: List every listening TCP port and every UDP endpoint with its local address and owning process (Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen and Get-NetUDPEndpoint, resolving OwningProcess to a process name). In the summary give the number of listening sockets and name the ports reachable from outside (bound to 0.0.0.0 or ::). Do not run follow-up commands on individual ports.
